answer: Proof-of-burn secures a decentralized cedar registry by requiring agents to permanently destroy tokens to mint identity credentials. Validators inspect ledger proofs for an unspendable transaction ember, forcing an attacker to incur a verifiable, non-recoverable capital loss for every forged node. While this mechanism sends a cost ripple through registration pools to deter mass attacks, it inherently favors well-funded entities and destroys circulating network liquidity.
